summary: Technical sync on marketplace listing and reference architecture for joint Redwood + AuroraCloud offering. Discussed packaging options (AMI/container, SaaS listing), billing/SKU mapping, networking/VPC constraints for private deployments, reference arch components (Redwood Private, Dedicated pools, KV cache, autoscaling), security/compliance checkpoints, and POC steps + timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is the Redwood x Aurora marketplace and reference arch sync. We have about 45 minutes. Quick intros?
[00:08] Sofia Ruiz: Hi, Sofia here, partner PM at AuroraCloud.
[00:12] Derek Lang: Derek, integrations lead.
[00:14] Aisha Khan: Aisha, marketplace eng.
[00:17] Tom Becker: Tom, security.
[00:21] Liam Chen: Liam from Redwood, solutions engineer.
[00:24] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda — marketplace listing format, reference arch for our private deployment and a joint POC plan.
[00:35] Sofia Ruiz: Sounds good, our goal is to have a marketplace listing + reference arch we can both point customers to. The PMs want a go/no-go by mid-Jan.
[00:44] Maya Patel: Great. High level, Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace we usually offer container images or a marketplace-managed listing — do you have a preference?
[00:57] Aisha Khan: We prefer marketplace images or AMIs, but Aurora's preference is to list a managed SaaS option too where possible, so folks can subscribe directly. We'll need pricing SKU info.
[01:10] Liam Chen: Ok — we can do both. For the AMI/container path we provide an image plus an IaC example for quick install. For SaaS listing we provide the redirect and subscription flow; we'll also supply a usage billing SKU mapping (per-token / per-embedding).
[01:26] Derek Lang: On the private deployment side we need to understand network constraints — e.g., do you require VPC peering, NAT, or can you do private endpoints? Also what ports and IP ranges?
[01:38] Liam Chen: Good question. For Redwood Private we support customer-managed VPC with either VPC peering or VPC endpoints. We prefer private endpoints for data-plane traffic; management plane can be tunneled via our control plane or customer-hosted connectors depending on reqs.
[01:51] Tom Becker: From security, we need KMS integration and audit logs. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[01:58] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; we can offer customer-managed keys and ensure encrypted-at-rest with audit logs. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and our compliance pack.
[02:08] Aisha Khan: When you say audit logs, is that part of the console or a separate export?
[02:12] Liam Chen: It's exportable — Redwood Console has per-route tracing and audit logs; we can push logs to S3 or your SIEM (via syslog / event forwarding).
[02:22] Sofia Ruiz: On the marketplace listing, Aurora needs a short description, icons, screenshots, and a reference architecture diagram. Do you have a sample reference arch?
[02:31] Liam Chen: Yeah, we'll share a reference arch doc. It includes components: load balancer, Redwood serving runtime (in a dedicated pool or as part of Private nodes), KV cache for session prefix caching, model runtimes (container images or GPU AMIs), autoscaling policies, and optional inference caching.
[02:47] Derek Lang: About KV cache — is that per-tenant or shared?
[02:50] Liam Chen: Typically per-tenant; for dedicated pools we can colocate tenant caches or use a shared cache with strict RBAC. The transcription here is a bit fuzzy — sometimes our docs refer to it as "K-V cache" and sometimes people type "KV cache".
[03:02] Maya Patel: Also noted: model variants and quantization recommendations are in the Optimize playbook we'll attach. For marketplace customers we should include recommended defaults for batch sizes and quantization to control cost.
[03:14] Aisha Khan: For the listing, do you provide a managed billing integration to Aurora's marketplace so customers purchase via Aurora and Redwood gets invoiced?
[03:23] Maya Patel: Yes we can integrate with marketplace billing flows. We map subscriptions to our internal SKU and reconcile monthly. We'll need Aurora's billing API docs and sample webhook endpoints.
[03:33] Tom Becker: For regulated customers we need data residency guarantees. Can you pin a region or ensure logs don't leave region?
[03:40] Liam Chen: Yes — Redwood Dedicated/Private can be deployed in specific regions and we have controls for log retention and residency. We'll call out region pinning in the reference arch.
[03:50] Derek Lang: On the POC/perf side, we want to run benchmarks — end-to-end latency and throughput. What's your recommended methodology?
[03:57] Liam Chen: SE recommendation: run a small synthetic workload that mirrors your customer distribution (seq length, prompt patterns). We'll run baseline on Aurora dev region with Redwood runtime on a GPU instance, measure p95 latency at target concurrency, and test autoscaling behavior. I'll upload a perf checklist and scripts.
[04:15] Sophia Ruiz: (laughs) "Sophia" correction — oh sorry, Sofia.
[04:19] Liam Chen: No worries. Also note some product names get transcribed weird in shared notes — e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes shows up as "Redwood Dedicate" in auto-transcripts.
[04:30] Maya Patel: Real quick, competitors — Aurora PM asked if we have partners using CloudMart or NovaEdge marketplace flows. We do, but our integration with Aurora will be slightly different because of your marketplace workflows.
[04:42] Sofia Ruiz: Good to know. On the reference arch diagram: Aurora typically requires a diagram showing network flow, private endpoints, IAM roles, and a step-by-step install for the marketplace image. Can you provide a Terraform snippet?
[04:55] Liam Chen: Yes, we can include Terraform and Helm examples. We'll include an example VPC peering config and Security Group rules (port 443 for control plane, 10250 for runtime metrics, though exact ports vary).
[05:07] Derek Lang: About autoscaling — do you offer policy primitives, like scale-by-latency or scale-by-queue-depth?
[05:12] Liam Chen: We support autoscaling based on throughput, queue depth, and latency percentiles. Also we have burst capacity options for Dedicated pools. We'll include recommended thresholds in the ref arch doc.
[05:25] Aisha Khan: For the marketplace listing meta, what about images/screenshots? We want to show the Redwood Console and billing screenshots.
[05:31] Maya Patel: We'll send a marketing-approved screenshot pack and a short 30s demo GIF.
[05:35] Tom Becker: Compliance question again — will logs contain prompts or redacted? Some customers require prompt redaction for PII.
[05:42] Liam Chen: We support redaction and configurable logging levels. For regulated customers we recommend redaction at the ingestion point and only logging metadata. We'll document the options.
[05:52] Sofia Ruiz: Ok great. Timeline recap? Aurora needs the listing draft and ref arch to review by Nov 30 — is that doable?
[05:59] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll aim to send the marketplace draft and pricing SKU mapping by 2026-11-30. SE will run baseline perf and share results by 2026-12-03. Aurora will provide network constraints and IaC samples by 2026-12-07.
[06:12] Derek Lang: If we run into perf issues, what's the escalation path?
[06:15] Maya Patel: Escalation — SE -> Solutions Engineering -> Engineering on-call. We'll include contacts in the follow-up email.
[06:22] Liam Chen: One last technical note — for model serving on Aurora we recommend the following: use quantized model variants for general-purpose workloads to cut cost, reserve dedicated GPU pools for low-latency SLA customers, and enable prefix caching for chat workloads to reduce repeated context compute.
[06:38] Aisha Khan: Noted.
[06:40] Maya Patel: Alright let's recap next steps: we'll share the docs, Terraform snippets, screenshots, and compliance artifacts. Schedule follow-up for week of Dec 7.
[06:50] Sofia Ruiz: Thanks everyone.
[06:52] Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
topics: security & compliance (KMS, audit logs, data residency)
